text:
Alex: Heads-up — onboarding sample app started spiking 429s during our weekend soak. Looks like client-side leaky-bucket + circuit-breaker combo is dropping bursts instead of smoothing. Anyone else seen this in JS SDK?
Maria: I saw similar in a customer repro yesterday but thought it was auth token churn. Did you correlate with refreshes?
Alex: Good call. Correlated with token refresh window — refresh triggered ~50 concurrent retry attempts that bypassed the leaky-bucket window and immediately tripped the circuit-breaker.
Jon: Oof. So two layers fighting: leaky-bucket should limit outgoing rate but our token-refresh path creates a flood that short-circuits it.
Sasha: Is this parity across SDKs? Go SDK uses a global limiter, JS SDK uses per-client limiter AFAIK. That could explain the different behaviors.
Alex: Yup — confirmed. Go: single token bucket, JS: per-conn buckets + a circuit-breaker that flips fast.
Maria: Suggestion: move token refresh to a low-priority queue that inherits the main limiter or add a small jittered backoff for refresh-triggered retries.
Jon: Also we should expose a "refresh_affinity" flag in SDK so apps can opt to serialize refreshes. Right now default is parallelism=5 which becomes 50 when many connections open.
Sasha: I pushed a quick patch to keep the leaky-bucket central in the adapter layer (so all clients share it). Patch: `adapter.rateLimiter = new SharedLeakyBucket({rate: 1000, burst: 200})` — but need tests.
Alex: Can you drop a repro? I made a script that simulates 100 clients opening simultaneously and forcing token expiry. Repro attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/rw/mock-repro (simulated)
Jon: Small code snippet for the proposed shared limiter and circuit break config we discussed:
```
// pseudo
const shared = new LeakyBucket({tokensPerSec: 200, burst: 50})
client.on('refresh', async () => {
  await shared.acquire(1)
  await wait(randomJitter(50, 200))
  return doRefresh()
})
// circuit breaker: open after 5 failures in 1s, cool down 2s
const cb = new CircuitBreaker({threshold: 5, windowMs: 1000, cooldownMs: 2000})
```
Sasha: We also need telemetry sampling — don't record every single 429 during high churn or we'll flood logs. Add sampling tags like `sample_rate=0.05` for high-frequency errors.
Maria: Agreed. We can add an event sampler on the SDK to send 5% of high-rate 429s plus all unique error types.
ci-bot: [CI] test-run/refresh-throttle-shared-limiter started (job #482) :gear: 
Alex: For immediate mitigation: update hosted quickstart sampleapp to set `tokenRefresh = "serialized"` and bump leaky-bucket burst down to 20. That should stop weekend soak from taking down the canary.
Sasha: I'll open a PR against SDK repo with tests + changelog note. Will also add a short migration guide for folks running multi-conn sample apps.
Jon: Long term: consider a server-side advisory header like `x-client-rate-hint` so SDKs can adapt local windows to server quotas.
Maria: +1 on rate-hint header — reduces mismatch between server quota and client heuristics.
Alex: Cool. Action items: Sasha PR (adapter shared limiter) / Maria telemetry sampler / Jon rate-hint design doc. I'll update the sampleapp quickstart now.
deploy-bot: Release note: quickstart sampleapp config updated (canary) — rollout planned at 02:00 UTC.
Alex: Thanks all — looping in @SRE if anything spikes after the canary. :thumbsup:
